thesis: A sudden seven-percent jump in one city's labour force left the wages of less-skilled workers already there essentially unchanged.
outsider_brief: It is the reference case for asking whether a large, sudden inflow of workers lowers the wages of the people already there.
author_abstract: This paper uses an unexpected arrival of migrants in one port city to study how a sudden increase in labour supply affects the wages and unemployment of workers already living there. Comparing the city with four similar cities, I find that the arrival had virtually no effect on the wages or unemployment rates of less-skilled incumbents.
